newsitem.title: USA: IMF chief sees agreement on SDR issue by spring.
newsitem.headline: IMF chief sees agreement on SDR issue by spring.

text.p: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus voiced hopes on Thursday the organization can reach agreement by the spring on a plan to issue Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) to its member nations.
"I trust that a final agreement will be reached in good faith before the spring meetings," he told the closing session of the joint IMF/World Bank annual meeting.
By issuing SDRs, the IMF basically creates money out of thin air, beefing up member nations' reserves and freeing up finances for use elsewhere.
Camdessus has proposed a 26 billion SDR allocation, mainly aimed at benefitting countries that have joined the IMF since the last issue in 1981.
But some industrial nations have opposed that as too large.
The SDR is currently worth about $1.44.
